subject.title: [Feature]: Optimization for Dockerfile.sandbox-common # add retries and fix-missings for apt-get

question: Should the sandbox APT resilience fix be retry-only, or may it include --fix-missing with explicit package verification and an accepted partial-install contract?
rationale: VISION.md supports setup reliability work, but the APT contract check shows --fix-missing changes failure semantics beyond retrying transient fetches, so maintainers need to choose the permanent sandbox image contract.

options.title: Retry-only Dockerfile change
options.body: Keep Acquire::Retries for transient network resilience and remove --fix-missing so required sandbox packages still fail closed after retries.

options.title: Accept --fix-missing with verification
options.body: Keep the flag only if maintainers intentionally accept partial-install semantics and require package-presence checks plus clear recovery behavior.

options.title: Defer the Docker reliability tweak
options.body: Leave the current fail-closed Dockerfiles unchanged until a maintainer sponsors a broader sandbox image build reliability policy.

recommendation.title: Retry-only Dockerfile change
recommendation.body: Keep Acquire::Retries for transient network resilience and remove --fix-missing so required sandbox packages still fail closed after retries.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent sandbox-common Dockerfile and setup-script maintenance makes this the best available routing candidate for the package-install contract choice.
